performers.role: Plastik-Kommando in der Spielzeugkiste, hält Wrestling für Fake und sich für den einzigen echten Kämpfer

structure: TRIPLET-SET t1 (Georg 21.10.): erst die Triplets als Aussagen, 90 % Kartentext. Ganzes Deck in Kartenreihenfolge, Intro und Outro = gedruckter Cover-Text, noch keine Brücken.
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about the psychology of professional wrestling. It is performed by a toy figure in its home, a toy box, for whoever happens to be there.
beats: Big Bad Brain Wrestling: the physics of fake pain and the economy of real ego.

beats.text: The Babyface, high-flying moves because audiences cheer. Cheat, you lose. A slave to approval.
The Heel cheats: bear hugs, eye pokes. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener, Face or Heel on a coin: you don't ask for it, which makes them want you more.
The Jobber exists to make the other guy look good. Only control: who defeats you.
The Immovable Object, slow gorilla, hurls you like a ragdoll. Shorthand: You Can't Win.
The Aerial Ace dodges any attack; fail, double damage. If you stand still, you die.
The Powerhouse Botch leaps off the top rope: crush yourself or everyone. Tragedy waiting.
The Little Giant, smaller wrestler, lifts the huge: surprise doubles damage.
The Master Seller converts damage into sympathy: reel back, limp, make them believe.
The No-Sell Monster sits right back up to prove how dangerous: removes all tension for ego.
The Oversell Clown reacts far beyond reality: a mockery of the sport. See: Michaels and Hogan.
The Limb Target, called shot: legs, no speed; arms, no lifting. Cruel, logical, effective.
The Thigh Slap didn't hurt, but sounds like it did: a loud sound, an audio lie.
The Stomp Punch stomps on the mat when punching: stun with noise. Kinetic misdirection.
The Echo Chest, echo chamber of the torso: loud, but many strikes to bruise.
The Chop Fest, nothing but chop until one quits. No other moves. A test of endurance.
The Sacred Mask, kayfabe sacred to identity: never remove it. If unmasked, game over.
The Rudo Ripper maims the mask: instant disqualification, but you win the feud.
The Strong Style Spirit: the more damage you take, the harder you hit back. Convey envy through pain.
The Limp Arm refuses the lockup: sign of a shooter. No help for inferior opponents.
The Juice Lover, busting himself open: you can't hurt me if I hurt me first.
The Snake Bag has a live snake: terrify them before the match starts.
The Lazy Genius, hands in pockets, looks like a chore: the apathy makes them furious.
The Exotic attacks dignity rather than the body: psychological dominance.
The Hot Tag, fresh partner for payback: the explosive release of tension.
The Victim, the Ricky Morton role: isolated and picked apart. You are the bait.
The Wolfpack, brawler, flyer, powerhouse: triple attack on the isolated. The numbers game.
The Savant Manager knows the moves better than they do: a night off for the opponent.
The Pop Hunter: if they want a heel, give them a heel. If they want a clown, honk your nose.
The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes: silence amplifies the sound of impacts.
The Green Screen Crowd pipes in noise to hide the emptiness: audio sweetening on a lie.
The Plant: I'm just a fan! Gambling on the outcome while part of the show.
The Shooter forces you to sell; if you refuse, real damage. Stiff the no-seller.
The Sandbag refuses to cooperate: dead weight. Extremely unprofessional.
The Real Injury, unplanned: Goldberg's shoulder, ring-post. Crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Cue Card Holder reveals the next move: short cuts for out-of-depth wrestlers.
The Undead Wizard gets under their skin before the match, with smoke and mirrors.
The Uninterested Genius: do as little as possible, then lash out at the crowds who ignored you.
The Trash Talker, shouting at Michael Cole: hilarious and entertaining abuse.
The Finger Poke of Doom: instant pin if you consent. Strength? No, gullibility.
The Finisher, the Leg Drop: the most important moment. If this hits, go home.
The False Finish survives the pinfall: an exciting comeback. The art of the near-fall.
The Squash against any jobber: no-selling, sit right back up. Total dominance.
The Time Limit Draw: no winner, both keep dignity. Strong style means no one loses.
The Booker decides the winner before it starts: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.
The Spot Caller changes the plan mid-match: a basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Rehearsal, Hogan and Warrior: perfect, but lacks soul. It paid off.
The Rest Hold: slow down, give the audience a chance to catch up. Or go get popcorn.
The Hard Cam plays to the crowd at home: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Ring Post, unforgiving steel, hardest object in the building: miss a charge, max damage.
The Steel Steps, weaponized furniture: counts as environment, not weapon. Usually.
The Announcer's Table: shouting at Michael Cole while destroying his desk. Breakable furniture.
The Internet Smark critiques bad psychology without ever taking a bump: keyboard warriors.
The Botched Spot, incoherent collection of moves: confusion. It just looks messy.
The Kayfabe Police enforce the lie: keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Retirement Match loses on purpose: rising and falling. See you next season.

beats: Don't try this at home. Try it at work.
